historicalReferences: Remember 1971? Peter Gethin's incredible victory, separated by just 0.61 seconds across the top five!
Ascari's tragic accident in 1955 forever changed the landscape of motorsport safety and cast a shadow over this legendary circuit.
Who can forget Schumacher's dominant years here, a masterclass of speed and precision at the Temple of Speed?
The 2000 Italian Grand Prix, a chaotic race marked by a first-lap pileup after a startline collision.
In 1988, Ferrari's Berger and Alboreto delivered a stunning 1-2 finish just weeks after Enzo Ferrari's death, a poignant moment for the Tifosi.
The 1961 Italian Grand Prix saw Wolfgang von Trips' fatal accident, a stark reminder of the dangers faced by drivers in the early days of Formula 1.
Senna's victory in 1990, a display of relentless determination and skill, cementing his place as a true legend.
The infamous chicane controversies of the past, attempts to tame the raw speed of Monza and improve safety.
In 2008, Sebastian Vettel, driving for Toro Rosso, took his maiden Grand Prix victory in wet conditions, a sign of things to come.
Hamilton's strategic masterclass in 2018, holding off Raikkonen despite immense pressure, a testament to his skill and the Mercedes' pace.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this abrasive Monza surface. Expect to see some teams struggling with blistering, especially on the soft compounds.
With such long straights, fuel consumption is critical. Managing fuel load will be key to maximizing performance.
The pit lane here at Monza is relatively long, so pit stops will cost more time than at other circuits. This can impact strategy decisions.
Overtaking opportunities are plentiful, but getting the timing right is crucial. The slipstream effect is incredibly powerful here.
A one-stop strategy is likely to be the preferred option, but safety cars can always throw a wrench into the works.
The optimal pit window will depend on tire wear and fuel consumption, but expect teams to be looking at laps 20-30.
With high-speed corners and long straights, mechanical reliability is paramount. Any issues could be devastating.
The long straights reward low-drag setups, but teams must also find a balance to maintain cornering speed in the Ascari and Lesmo sections.
weatherCommentary: The weather in Monza can be unpredictable, with sunshine one minute and rain the next. The proximity to the Alps can bring sudden showers.
A tailwind on the main straight could significantly increase top speeds, making overtaking even more exciting.
If the wind picks up from the east, it could affect the car's stability through the high-speed corners.
The temperature is rising, which will increase tire degradation. Teams will need to monitor this closely.
Rain in Monza can create chaos. The long straights become incredibly treacherous, and aquaplaning is a real risk.
